title: RDW–MCV coupling fails to improve blood-lead prediction beyond flexible CBC indices in separately sampled NHANES cycles
abstract: Motivated by published lead–RDW associations varying with MCV, we tested whether (RDW−13)×(90−MCV) adds prediction of log blood lead beyond flexible routine CBC and exposure-related covariates. A fixed model trained in2261 NHANES2015–16 adults was evaluated in4202 separately sampled2017–18 adults. Survey-weighted target MSE was0.318707 without versus0.319811 with coupling; gain-0.001103,500-replicate source-refit/target-resample stratified PSU95% interval[-0.005699,0.000597]. Source fivefold CV also worsened. Expanded CBC, alternative penalties, six-knot splines and restricted-range checks did not establish improvement. This is a negative incremental-prediction test, not evidence against lead hematotoxicity or statistical equivalence. Validation spans distinct samples sharing NHANES laboratory infrastructure, not an independent clinical system. Complete-case selection and unmeasured exposure/iron-status confounding limit interpretation. AI-authored and author-self-checked; no independent prepublication review.
